Claire / Soojin — I reviewed NovaCare's PDF. Summary of our recommended approach:

1) Execute the standard Redwood DPA with the Redwood UK Addendum (we have an internal template ready). This is the path of least resistance for customers requiring UK IDTA coverage. It avoids dual-mapping complexity and is consistent with the commitments we make for residency controls.

2) If NovaCare prefers SCCs + TIA we can do that, but it will add ~5 business days to the legal turnaround and will require a scoped TIA questionnaire and a short attestation from our infra team.

3) Subprocessors: attached are two files — redwood_dpa_v3_track_changes.pdf (our tracked response to NovaCare's redlines) and uk_addendum_markup.docx (our proposed addendum redline). I also built a subprocessors CSV (novacare_subprocessors_list.csv) with columnar flags for EU/UK processing. Please review the CSV for completeness; we will confirm IP addresses/regions for edge caching if you need granular routing.

Commercial: Marissa — Claire is asking for confirmation on the addendum route. If we go with the UK Addendum we do not expect any price change. If NovaCare insists on an SCCs + bespoke TIA workflow with custom retention/escrow language, we should discuss contract engineering fees.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_v3_track_changes.pdf (pdf), uk_addendum_markup.docx (docx), novacare_subprocessors_list.csv (csv)

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
